summary: This Wikipedia list table shows the territorial entities where German is an official language, with 2014/2015 population figures and estimated numbers of native and second-language speakers for each. It covers Germany, Belgium, Austria, Switzerland, Luxembourg and Liechtenstein, notes each country's official-status arrangement, and gives totals for the group.
one_line: Table of six territories where German is an official language, with population and native and second-language speaker estimates.
key_facts: Germany has a 2014/2015 population of 81,083,600, with an estimated 74,430,000 (91.8%) native German speakers and 5,600,000 (6.9%) second-language speakers.
Germany is listed as the sole nationwide official language of Germany.
Belgium has a population of 11,245,629, with an estimated 73,000 (0.6%) native German speakers and 2,472,746 (22%) second-language speakers.
German is a de jure nationwide co-official language in Belgium and is the majority language only in the German speaking community.
Austria has a population of 8,602,112, with an estimated 7,999,964 (93%) native German speakers and 516,000 (6%) second-language speakers.
German is the de jure sole nationwide official language of Austria.
Switzerland has a population of 8,256,000, with an estimated 5,329,393 (64.6%) native German speakers and 395,000 (5%) second-language speakers.
In Switzerland German is a co-official language at federal level, is the sole official language in 17 cantons and co-official in 4 cantons, out of 26.
Luxembourg has a population of 562,958, with an estimated 11,000 (2%) native German speakers and 380,000 (67.5%) second-language speakers.
German is a de jure nationwide co-official language in Luxembourg.
Liechtenstein has a population of 37,370, with an estimated 32,075 (85.8%) native German speakers and 5,200 (13.9%) second-language speakers.
German is the de jure sole nationwide official language of Liechtenstein.
Across the six listed entities the total population is 109,787,669, with 87,875,432 native German speakers and 9,368,946 second-language speakers.
The table gives a total of 97,244,378 German speakers across the listed entities.
